items.stem: Why do historians treat the two world wars as connected but not a single inevitable conflict?

options.text: The 1919 settlement and interwar choices shaped the second war, but different decisions could have altered outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: the wars are linked through contingent decisions, not a predetermined single event.

options.text: Because the wars happened in the same year
Because they involved none of the same countries
options.rationale: Many of the same states fought; the point is about inevitability.

options.text: Because there was no connection at all
options.rationale: There were real connections; the caution is against inevitability.

items.explanation: Correct: the wars are linked through contingent decisions, not a predetermined single event.

Correct: sustained anti-colonial movements pressed for and won independence.

options.text: The invention of the printing press
The fall of the Roman Empire

items.stem: A commentator argues that globalisation is 'entirely new and benefits everyone equally'. What is the flaw?

options.text: Global connection has a long history and its gains and costs are distributed unevenly
options.rationale: Correct: globalisation is not wholly new and produces winners and losers, not uniform benefit.
It is a real process; the issue is the claim about it.

options.text: Trade began only in the 21st century

options.rationale: Some benefit substantially; the point is uneven distribution.
